question.problem:
An arithmetic sequence ${a}_{n}$ is defined by 

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+15,\,{a}_{1}=0,\,n\ge 1?
$$

The $6$th term of this sequence is{{field-1}}.

current_example.problem:
Calculate the fourth term of the sequence

$$
f(n+1) = f(n) -6, \quad f(1) = 1, \quad n\geq 1.
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
Starting with the first term $f(1)=1,$ we compute the next terms using the recursive rule until we reach the fourth term $f(4).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =1 \\ f(2) & =f(1)-6=1-6=-5 \\ f(3) & =f(2)-6=-5-6=-11 \\ f(4) & =f(3)-6=-11-6=-17\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fourth term is $f(4)=-17.$
